newsitem.title: USA: Life USA '97 EPS could surpass estimates.
newsitem.headline: Life USA '97 EPS could surpass estimates.

text.p: LifeUSA Holding Inc has the potential to beat the Street earnings consensus of $1.07 per share for 1997, chairman Robert MacDonald told Reuters after the company's annual shareholders meeting.

"I'm comfortable with where the analysts are today ($1.07 earnings per share for 1997) and I'm encouraged that we have the potential to do better than that, given our first-quarter results and today's environment, and where we appear to be trending," MacDonald said.
The company, which markets financial services, earned $1 per share in 1996.
On Monday, LifeUSA reported first-quarter earnings of $0.22 per share, up from $0.21 in the same year-ago period. Revenues rose to $79.4 million, up from $73.6 million.
MacDonald said the company may issue new shares for acquisitions that would add to earnings.

"There could be an increase in the number of shares, depending upon how many of these marketing organizations we may invest in. We're negotiating with five or six right now. I wouldn't be surprised to see two or three of these close in the second quarter," MacDonald said.

"Most of them will be a minority interest. We could use stock to help us acquire some, but the increase in the number of shares issued will be accretive because we'd be acquiring the revenues of these marketing organizations," he said.

MacDonald also said he would not be surprised to see a 20 percent increase in sales, and a similar increase in revenues. "Since 75 percent of the business we write is sold to reinsurers who pay us revenues, if we get a 20 percent increase in sales, you're going to get a similar increase in revenues. I would not be surprised to see that kind of increase in sales," he said.

The executive said he expects retail revenues from LifeUSA Securities by the third quarter. "LifeUSA Securities was launched as a wholesale broker-dealer late last year. But approval to do retail came in yesterday from the NASD (National Association of Securities Dealers Inc). It'll take us a little while to gear up, but we'll probably do the first retail revenues in the third quarter," he noted.
MacDonald said he expected operating expenses to increase slower than revenues in 1997, contrary to 1996 and the first quarter of 1997 when operating expenses rose twice as fast as revenues.
